frozen_packaging.title: Burgers, Lipstick & Underwear
frozen_packaging.subtitle: What Strange Indicators Really Tell Us About the Economy
frozen_packaging.primary_reader: Curious general nonfiction readers who like popular economics, data stories, strange comparisons and practical skepticism without technical math.
frozen_packaging.reader_promise: Ordinary objects and strange indicators can make large economic and social systems readable, but the reader will learn which measures illuminate and which are mostly myth, incentive or meme.
frozen_packaging.cover_territory: Object-led popular nonfiction built around burger, lipstick and underwear. No dashboards, corporate data-platform aesthetic, owner-project branding or generic AI imagery.

book_thesis: Humans invent indices because reality is too large to hold in the head. A burger, an hour of work, a tube of lipstick or a ship full of grain can turn abstraction into something familiar enough to argue with. That translation is powerful: it can reveal purchasing power, confidence, risk, fragility and manipulation faster than official language can. But a vivid proxy is also dangerous. Some strange measures are grounded and useful; others survive because they are funny, flattering or convenient. This book is about learning to enjoy the strange measures without being fooled by them.

chapter_context_contract.purpose: Provide the minimum chapter-specific material needed to draft one chapter without rereading all historical audits or the full source document.
generation_inputs: source metadata and resolved P0/P1 checks
prohibited_behavior: Do not dump raw corpus paragraphs into the chapter prompt.
Do not treat Perplexity/source-pack summaries as final authority where an underlying source exists.
Do not include owner-project promotional material unless it adds unique editorial context.

chapter_loop: resolve P0 and chapter-relevant P1 evidence
manuscript_v1_production_plan.human_approval_policy: Do not require per-chapter approval unless a material factual, rights, scope or voice issue appears.
acceptance_criteria: voice reasonably consistent with Voice Contract
citations and source notes retained internally

research_during_writing.strategy: Verify according to manuscript need, not by front-loading all 388 URLs.
priority_order: P0 before claim appears in manuscript
P2 only when the example survives into prose
research_during_writing.rag_reason: Chapter-specific ContextPacks can be built deterministically from structured corpus files, chapter mapping, source metadata and the verification queue.

visual_policy.style: Conventional commercial nonfiction, not a discovery booklet.
avoid: excessive color dependency that harms paperback economics
visual_policy.print_constraint: Visuals should work in grayscale where practical.
visual_policy.rights_constraint: No external image/screenshot inclusion without rights review.

format_plan.interior: Black-and-white by default; use color only if later visual QA proves commercial value.
format_plan.typography_direction: Readable popular nonfiction serif body with compact charts/tables; not a design-heavy art book.
format_plan.kindle_risk: Keep visuals simple and separately described so Kindle reflow is not broken by complex layout.

owner_project_rule.allowed: 1D3X / POP / SPIKE may appear only if author experience adds unique editorial value.
owner_project_rule.acceptable_voice: I encountered this problem while building an index.

ignore_by_default_for_004: all historical Book Factory audits before BOOK-FACTORY-INDICES-003
owner-project promotional material unless directly relevant to a chapter claim
context_economy.expected_reduction: 004 should start from five compact canonical files plus targeted corpus lookup, avoiding broad audit rereads and raw-document reprocessing.
